## Part 2 — migratory-sharing optimization (read miss → GetX), 4 cores, one read→write pair each

| metric                       | base (coherence_opt=0) | opt (coherence_opt=1) |
|------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| GetS sent                    | 4                      | 0                     |
| GetX sent                    | 4                      | 4                     |
| invalidations seen           | 6                      | 0                     |
| interventions                | 3                      | 0                     |
| recorded transitions         | 6                      | 0                     |
| S->I                         | 3                      | 0                     |
| M->S                         | 2                      | 0                     |
| M->I                         | 1                      | 0                     |
| S->M (counter)               | 0                      | 0                     |
| **bus requests (GetS+GetX)** | 8                      | 4                     |

Note: `S->M` reads 0 in **both** runs. The base upgrade goes S → SM → M through a transient state that `recordTransition` does not canonicalise, so that counter never fires. The upgrade evidence is `GetX sent` (one per core in base, for the write after the read) and `S->I` on the other sharers. Do not cite "S->M 0" as a result.

Not in these files: cycle counts for base vs opt. `run-prospero-traces.py` filtered stdout to `Counter[` lines only, so the SST `stateEvent_*` statistics and the simulated time were discarded before the `.out` was written.
